# 1.2.113 - Facilities: the Rest tile becomes Facilities, with the rests and the actions of the room a character stands in - a GM's room actions set in Room Setup and rolled on the GMs' record, a completed project's action for its lifetime - and five new Despair Overflow states

Stage E93 alone, built on one work line from 1.2.105's line (f22a7e87). Its commits are C1 ee59a46, C6
5deb505, C3 afdc430, C2+C4 c0ad643 and the STATUS 0590271; two later parts sit after E69's and E74's commits on the
same line: df3ffb6 (a fixture of an older test, E15-T4, below) and the room action's branch of E74 C7's Reroll
replays (68ec08d). In plain words:

- **The Facilities tile.** The tile that held Short Rest and Long Rest is named **Facilities** in English and Polish
  (its key stays `rest`). Inside it: the two rests, as before, and the actions of the room the character stands in.
- **A GM's room actions.** In Room Setup, the Rest tab is the **Facilities** tab: beside the two rest columns, a
  **Room actions** column with each room's count and an edit button. Each action has a name, a statistic, a
  difficulty and up to four effects (Health, Sanity, Hope, a search token, a Free Move, Hope for another present,
  minus the Overflow counter, text from the GM, a story effect, among others). A player's use is rolled: the roll is
  drawn on the primary GM's browser, its statistic the GMs' copy of the action's, and the effects are written there.
  A GM's action may be used by one person per time of day; once anyone uses it, a failed roll too, it is closed for
  everyone until the next time of day. Every use of a GM's action leaves a faint Subtle trace.
- **A completed project's action.** In the project manager, a button in a project's Edit cell (after the pen) sets
  the action a completed project gives: its name, its effects, whether it costs an action (default yes) and its
  lifetime (indefinite, or a number of days). It is offered in the project's room, with no roll, once per person per
  time of day. The Projects window's line of a completed project names its room action and the time left.
- **Five new Overflow states**, in Despair Flow's Overflow tab: **Lockdown** (room actions off for the time of day),
  **Insomnia** (no Short Rest), **Toll** (room actions cost one more action), **Jitters** (room action rolls at
  disadvantage) and **Power cut** (actions from completed projects off for the time of day). They start unticked:
  out of the hat until a GM ticks them (a default, below).

Nothing in this version ran at a real table or on a Foundry server; what was measured was measured headless. Below,
an R number names one of the module's own tests (`game.drpg.runTests()`), and a scenario one of the headless
harness's multi-browser runs.

## Before installing

- **No world migration.** No clause was added to `migrate.mjs`, and no language key of the module's was removed or
  renamed. The tile's label changes to Facilities in both languages; its key and the rests' settings stay.
- **New stored data**: one world setting, `facilityClosed` (the GM's room actions closed for the time of day, by
  their key; `config: false`), and one GM store, `facilityUses` (who used which action and when, kept in the GMs'
  browsers). A secret project's action is kept in the GMs' half while the project is secret.
- **The Overflow hat**: the five new states are not drawn until a GM ticks them in Despair Flow. A table that changes
  nothing draws from the same states as before.

## The bridge road `facility.use` (E93 C3 afdc430)

- A row of the bridge's table, built by the five steps of a bridge action: the sender owns the character, no undo in
  a player's packet, the roll named off the GMs' record (`rolled`, kind `facility`), the action looked up in the room
  the GMs hold the character in. Lockdown and Power cut refuse; a GM's action with no roll is refused while the GMs
  draw; the limit is judged and written in one step; a project's price is taken by the GM. `facility` is a new write
  reason, a GM's alone. roll-draw.mjs: no draw for an action not in the room or closed, Jitters' die of disadvantage.
- Red first: E93-T2 at 5deb505 with the test alone, failed (no `facility.use` in the table); green with the road.
- Tiers 0-1 whole: "1157 passed, 5 failed" (R1239, R218, R472, R291, R1157, each a census of this stage's new names,
  fixed), then "1161 passed, 1 failed" (R1448, a line's wording, fixed), green alone after.
- Scenario 33 E93-A, the legal control from p1's page: first read Hope 3 and 4 where the check asked 2 and 3 (the
  check's mistake: a roll with Hope gives its own Hope); green after, 74/74. Scenario 30, "the forged packets of a room action"
  (another's character, an action of another room, no roll, a roll that does not exist; the draw): green, both checks
  measured.
- CI on afdc430 (run 43142590218): failure; its log was not read (E15-T4's fixture was in the tree, above).

## A Reroll of a Facilities roll (part of E74 C7, 68ec08d)

- Until 68ec08d, a Reroll of a room action's roll fell to reroll.mjs's `default`: the GMs were told "this roll left no
  lasting effect" and the first result stood. Now infiltrate-reroll.mjs `settleFacility` replays it on the primary GM
  from the facts the GMs' run wrote on the roll's row: a failure rerolled into a success applies the action's effects;
  a success stands (its effects were given), and the line says so.
- Red first: E74-T6 and E74-T7 on a worktree of a123ff1 with only tests-tier2.mjs copied in, every case the no-replay
  line; on the tree "6 passed". The numbers for the whole commit are in 1.2.115's notes.

## The owner's answers

- **05.11.2026**, the audit entry (as the plan records it, translated): the Rest tile becomes the Facilities tile; two
  sources of room actions (a GM's in Room Setup, rolled; a completed project's, no roll); a project gets a lifetime;
  a wide list of effects; the five Overflow states, "Sabotage and Spoilage rejected". The same day: a failed roll
  uses the action for that time of day; option A, the Projects tile stays separate and completed projects' actions are
  in Facilities; the limits - a project's action once per person per time of day, a GM's action one person per time of
  day and closed for everyone once used.
- **08.11.2026**: a project's action may cost no action if the GM sets so, a switch per action, default yes.
- **12.11.2026**, on the shots of E93, E69 and E74, as the coordinator relayed it: "na razie wygladaja dobrze". No
  changes asked.
- Defaults taken in the work, each the owner's to revise (docs/dev/e93/STATUS.md): the "costs an action" switch is a
  completed project's action's only, Work keeps its cost (Q-E93-1); a room's GM actions are listed only to a character
  standing in the room (Q-E93-2); Toll raises the room actions only, not the rests (Q-E93-4); "for those present" is
  read on the GM at the moment of use (Q-E93-5); a GM's action leaves a faint Subtle trace, a project's action and the
  rests none (Q-E93-6); the five new states start unticked; a Relief's free Short Rest is not barred by Insomnia; a
  GM's room action always costs an action; the tile's hint, the owner's approved text of batch B01a, is left as it
  was and speaks of the rests only; the project manager's new button sits in the Edit cell, no new column; a secret
  project's insiders are not offered its action while it is secret.

## Known gaps

- **Not built**: the effects that need a mechanism the module does not have - an item's durability, a state removed,
  temporary +X to a trait, a temporary Experience, advantage on the next trait roll, a stronger next ultimate Hope Call,
  protection from Despair on a roll, a crossing in an Eclipse, project progress (it needs a pick of the project). No
  timed effect exists to extend. Q-E93-3 (the timed effects' length) is not reached.
- **No scenario of the stage's own**: scenario 33's E93-A, 30's forged packets and the tier-2 tests cover the roads.
- **Watched, not caught**: under Toll a GM's action costs 2 actions; the roller's browser pays both before the roll,
  and the GM's draw sees one payment, not its size. A console paying one under Toll rolls all the same.
- **A room's GM actions are region flags**, which every browser holds: a console reads them anywhere, the same as a
  room's description today.
- **The look** was seen in Chromium on the harness's pages (audit/style-harness.html), both themes, EN and PL, at
  1366x768: not Foundry, no Font Awesome, no Foundry window frame. Seen there and left as it is: the rests' sentence
  "No room on this map is marked for a yet", an older text with an empty `{kind}`, not this stage's.
- **Scenario 61's D5**, "the same browser back in world A reads its traces intact, and no GM had to send it a
  section": measured, not this line's code. Alone it passed 5 times of 5 on the line's last commit; two runs of 61 at
  once failed at that commit and at older ones of the line (f64d5f6 among them, which CI passed); at f22a7e87 one run
  alone passed. The section the GMs sent was the store `clockBeat`, the primary's periodic clock beat: when a beat
  lands while that browser is in world B, its copy of world A is one beat behind on its return.
